title: Japan’s Shimizu Invests in Noble Machines to Develop Humanoid Robots for Construction
key_facts: Shimizu Corporation, a Japanese construction company, has invested in Silicon Valley startup Noble Machines and launched a collaboration to develop humanoid robots for construction sites.
The robots are meant to assist with or replace workers in physically demanding and hazardous tasks.
Shimizu plans to begin virtual simulations by the end of this year using its building information modeling data; tests at real construction sites are scheduled to begin next spring.
First tasks: moving materials, navigating job sites and conducting patrols.
Noble Machines, based in Sunnyvale, California, was founded in May 2024, is led by CEO Wei Ding and develops the MOBY series of humanoid robots plus control software.
Shimizu points to an aging workforce and fewer young workers entering construction as a long-term labor pressure.
The article does not give the size of the investment.
quote_evidence: Shimizu Corporation has invested in Silicon Valley startup Noble Machines and launched a collaboration to develop humanoid robots for construction sites.
Shimizu plans to begin virtual simulations by the end of this year using its building information modeling and construction information modeling, or BIM/CIM, data.
Shimizu noted that the construction industry is facing longer-term labor pressures caused in part by an aging workforce and fewer younger workers entering the field.
why_it_matters_hint: A large Japanese builder is backing humanoid robots to cover a shrinking construction workforce, but real-site tests are still months away.
notes: Based on Shimizu's announcement as relayed by AI Insider; investment amount not given.
